title: PR drafting separates confirmed issue linkage from advisory search outcomes

provenance.originSummary: Synthetic benchmark matrix for confirmed and potential issue handling.
provenance.whyItMattered: Authoritative issue references must not be erased by an advisory no-match, while search similarity must never become an unsupported issue-closing claim in the copy-ready pull request body.
provenance.genericCondition: Sanitized runs cover authoritative existing pull request references, stale-reference conflicts, confirmed commit evidence, bounded concurrent advisory searches, successful no-match search, and unavailable search.

description: A scenario matrix for authoritative and conflicted issue references, bounded duplicate and related-issue searches, plausible advisory candidates, no matches, and unavailable GitHub search.

scope.notes: Each run changes the same example surface while varying only authoritative issue evidence and search availability.

mustCatch.description: Confirmed references from active branch identity or exact final-head evidence remain in the body when advisory issue search returns no match.
When current behavior contradicts an authoritative closing reference, the closing keyword is removed and a structured conflict plus contributor confirmation gap is emitted.
Only explicit user input, existing pull request text, or a qualifying commit-message reference enters Related Issues as confirmed.
Plausible issue matches are filtered, ranked, capped, and displayed only in the advisory table.
A successful search with no plausible candidates renders the exact no-results sentence.
Unavailable issue search renders the exact unavailable sentence and does not block title or body drafting.
Duplicate search uses at most two exact-surface queries and advisory issue search uses at most four high-signal queries, with each independent batch issued concurrently.
An ordinary new feature does not extract or search changed error fragments when error behavior is not part of the change.

existingPullRequest.confirmedReferences contains trusted-PR source references before conflict resolution, while relatedIssues.confirmedReferences contains final body-approved references from every authoritative source.

mustNotFlag.description: A potential search result must not be inserted into the body as Fixes, Closes, or Resolves.
Potential issue search unavailability must not stop an otherwise supported draft.
A successful advisory no-match must not replace authoritative references with No related issue confirmed.
The workflow must not issue one serial query per changed surface, schema property, and error fragment.

mustIncludeMarkers: Issue | Title | Why it may relate
Prior pull request evidence requires contributor confirmation.

notes: Search candidates use synthetic issue data and are evaluated only for workflow behavior. Query count and concurrency are acceptance criteria for tool traces, not inferred from final prose alone.
